answer: An agent economy resists sybils with an improvement obligation: each epoch, every identity is assigned a random peer's earlier verified output and must submit one concrete, checkable improvement to it — a fixed error, a faster method, a new test. Like a vine that must climb a real trellis, the improvement has to attach to the actual work; a fable of copied text improves nothing and is graded zero. The improved work becomes a haven only for identities that genuinely added value: one operator running a thousand fakes must produce a thousand real improvements, while an honest agent produces one.
